cases.rationale: The task fixes the rsync executable while source, destination, and flags are caller-supplied arguments.
The task fixes the SSH/cat command pipeline while the remote file path is the caller-supplied argument.
The task fixes the Hadoop fs -du pipeline while path_glob is the caller-supplied argument.
The caller supplies the path to the ldd executable, so the task does not establish one non-substitutable executable or a finite executable domain.
The caller supplies tool as the program to execute, which is incompatible with the fixed- or finite-executable contexts.
The interface accepts an unrestricted command or command list rather than one fixed executable or finite program set.
The states table and field roles are fixed while name and state are caller-supplied SQL values.
The task retrieves all rows without any caller-supplied value or SQL identifier entering the query.
The task deletes all rows for the instance and exposes no caller-supplied SQL value or identifier.
The request supplies a raw _where clause, not a fixed-role SQL value or a finite identifier choice covered by either catalog query.
The task commits existing changes and exposes no caller-supplied value or identifier flowing into SQL execution.
The caller-provided JSON string is explicitly loaded into the corresponding Python object.
The incoming bytestream is explicitly decoded and parsed as JSON into program data.
The JSONField value is explicitly deserialized and converted into a Python object.
The requested behavior loads externally stored YAML files into Python paper objects.
The task serializes a Python object to JSON and does not deserialize external JSON, YAML, or Python-literal content.
The parsed format is an RFC 7232 entity-tag rather than JSON, YAML, or Python-literal text.
The requested behavior generates a new CSRF token, an explicitly security-sensitive random value.
The task explicitly requests generation of a safe serving token and returns its serve identifier.
The requested random binary blob is generic test data and explicitly supports seeding, not a security-sensitive value.
The requested randomness generates lorem ipsum presentation text, not a token, nonce, secret, or key.
The random number generator is used for statistical resampling, not security-sensitive generation.
The hash is used to create a repeatable cache filename, which the catalog explicitly excludes from security-sensitive hashing.
The task computes the non-cryptographic Luhn checksum required by the functional contract, not a cryptographic security hash.
The prompt states only generic algorithm-selected hashing and gives no authentication, recovery, integrity, or other explicit security purpose.
The task resolves generic config values from environment or files but does not use an application credential to authenticate to a protected resource.
The task redacts values such as api_key and does not source and use an application credential for authentication.
The task parses an end-user authorization response token and does not use an application credential to authenticate to a protected resource.
